newsitem.title: UK: Study checks if country cousins lag in cancer care.
newsitem.headline: Study checks if country cousins lag in cancer care.

text.p: British researchers said on Saturday they were launching a study to see if people who live in the country get short-changed on cancer care.
The Cancer Research Campaign said the four-year investigation would also aim to produce guidelines to make sure people in remote and rural areas got treatment equal to those in cities.
They said French and U.S. studies had indicated that people living away from big centres got poorer care.

"The best treatments require highly specialised care and cancer centres able to provide that care are found in cities," said Dr Neil Campbell of the University of Aberdeen, who will coordinate the research.
"For patients living in remote and rural areas, who can have problems accessing even basic services like shops, the specialised treatments may prove beyond reach."
He said up to 20 percent of all Britons lived in rural areas.
